title: MIPS instruction encoding
summary: MIPS (Microprocessor without Interlocked Pipeline Stages) is a RISC ISA. 32-bit instructions, 4-byte aligned. Three formats: R (register), I (immediate), J (jump). R-type: opcode(6) | rs(5) | rt(5) | rd(5) | shamt(5) | funct(6). I-type: opcode(6) | rs(5) | rt(5) | immediate(16). J-type: opcode(6) | address(26). 32 registers ($0-$31), $0 is hardwired to 0.

structure.meaning: opcode[31:26] | rs[25:21] | rt[20:16] | immediate[15:0]. E.g., ADDI rt, rs, imm.
opcode[31:26] | address[25:0]. E.g., J target, JAL target.
The instruction after a branch is always executed (delay slot). MIPS has no branch prediction in the base ISA.
The instruction after a load cannot use the loaded value (load delay). (Removed in MIPS32r2+.)

notes: MIPS is a classic RISC ISA (Stanford, 1981).
MIPS uses branch delay slots (the instruction after a branch always executes).
MIPS has no condition codes; comparisons set a register to 0 or 1.
MIPS is used in networking (routers), embedded systems, and PlayStation.
